{"metadata":{"description":"Remote Host Tunnel Manager for dsh: remote port allocation + registry + resilient SSH tunnel","id":"gh:1335115571","install_available":true,"language":"JavaScript","name":"dsh-remote-tunnel","slug":"Linjiangxian0203/dsh-remote-tunnel","topics":["deepseek","deepseek-harness","dsh-plugin","javascript","ssh"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Remote Host Tunnel Manager for dsh: remote port allocation + registry + resilient SSH tunnel"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-remote-tunnel"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"中文 | English"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"**Remote Host Tunnel Manager**: automates the "local browser → dsh web on a remote Linux server" lin"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"k — remote port allocation with a registry, systemd supervision, resilient SSH tunneling, local URL "},{"id":"p4s3","text":"output, and full lifecycle management. Built for single users and for teams sharing one server."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"- Sessions and files live **on the server** (the remote dsh web's workspace = server directories); t"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"he local machine only keeps a tunnel
- Each user automatically gets a **dedicated remote port**, dou"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"ble-checked on the server (real occupancy + registry) before allocation — safe under concurrency
- E"},{"id":"p5s4","text":"very allocation is **recorded in a registry on the server** (`/etc/dsh-ports.tsv`, or a per-user fal"},{"id":"p5s5","text":"lback depending on permissions) — `audit` compares the registry against real occupancy at any time
-"},{"id":"p5s6","text":" The tunnel **auto-reconnects** after network drops (backoff respawn), and heartbeats keep the regis"},{"id":"p5s7","text":"try fresh
- Occupied local ports shift automatically, with the occupying process reported"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## If you're just a user (not developing)"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"The remote server needs: Node ≥ 24.9, dsh, systemd, and key-based ssh login. **Every account** (each"},{"id":"p8s2","text":" labmate's own user) prepares its own environment once — idempotent, runs as whoever the ssh alias l"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"ogs in as:
`dsh --profile remote bootstrap lab` (same script, manual: `ssh <host> 'sh -s' < scripts/"},{"id":"p8s4","text":"bootstrap-remote.sh`). Everything else lives in `$DSH_HOME/remote-tunnel/config.yaml` — sensible def"},{"id":"p8s5","text":"aults, no changes needed."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"> The `remote` CLI profile is the main interface. Installing into the **web** profile is what makes "},{"id":"p9s2","text":"the plugin appear under **Settings → Plugins** and enables the `/remote` slash commands in chat — re"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"start `dsh web` once after adding it there."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"## Requirements"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"- Local: Windows/macOS/Linux with the built-in OpenSSH client (Windows 10+ ships it), **Node ≥ 22.19"},{"id":"p11s2","text":"**
- Remote: Linux, Node ≥ 24.9 + dsh (installable per account via `dsh --profile remote bootstrap <"},{"id":"p11s3","text":"host>` or `scripts/bootstrap-remote.sh` — each user runs it once for their own account; the floor tr"},{"id":"p11s4","text":"acks `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2`'s `engines.node`), systemd (user-level is enough — no root needed)
- R"},{"id":"p11s5","text":"ecommended: passwordless ssh key login (`ssh <alias>` connects without prompts)"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"## Install (development)"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"## Quick start"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"The local URL opens the dsh web **on the server**: chat and read/write server files. Configure the A"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"PI key in the remote web's Settings → Models (written to the server's `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` — t"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"his plugin and the tunnel never touch credentials)."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## Desktop app panel"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"Installed into the desktop profile, the remote dsh web opens **inside the right sidebar's Browser pa"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"nel** — no trip to the system browser. The plugin adds four entry points:"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"| Entry point | Where | What it gives you |"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"| **Remote connections panel** | Right sidebar → guide → 远程连接 | Host list, tunnel state and every ac"},{"id":"p20s2","text":"tion — **the entry that works in a brand-new session** |
| **Command card** | Type `/remote …` in a "},{"id":"p20s3","text":"conversation | The command's output plus tunnel state, with "Open in browser", "Open in sidebar", "S"},{"id":"p20s4","text":"tart tunnel / up" and "Disconnect / down" |
| **Status strip** | Above the composer | Always shows t"},{"id":"p20s5","text":"he tunnel state with one-click actions (hide it with `dock: false`) |
| **Plugins page** | Left side"},{"id":"p20s6","text":"bar → 插件 | Enable/disable the plugin; its title and description follow the UI language |"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"### The sidebar「远程连接」panel"},{"id":"p22s1","text":"The sidebar draws its tab strip and its guide in **every** session state, so this pane is the one en"},{"id":"p22s2","text":"try
that survives a conversation with no history: the command card needs transcript history, and the"},{"id":"p22s3","text":" status
strip is not rendered in the hero layout a new session shows."},{"id":"p23s1","text":"1. Open the right sidebar (the button in the conversation header, if it is collapsed).
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p24s1","text":"## How it works"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"1. **Remote port allocation (atomic)**: one remote script runs under a `flock` lock — read the regis"},{"id":"p25s2","text":"try's in-use set + probe every port in the range with a real bind → pick the first port free on both"},{"id":"p25s3","text":" sides → append a TSV row → echo the port. Concurrent allocators can never hand out the same port.
2"},{"id":"p25s4","text":". **Remote supervision**: writes a systemd unit and `enable --now`s it. With passwordless sudo it us"},{"id":"p25s5","text":"es a **system** unit (`/etc/systemd/system/dsh-web-<user>.service`); without sudo it automatically f"},{"id":"p25s6","text":"alls back to a **user** unit (`~/.config/systemd/user/dsh-web.service`) plus `loginctl enable-linger"},{"id":"p25s7","text":"` — no root required at all. Survives reboots and crashes.
3. **TOCTOU fallback**: if dsh loses a bi"},{"id":"p25s8","text":"nd race at startup (`EADDRINUSE` shows up in the unit journal), the port is added to the exclusion s"},{"id":"p25s9","text":"et and the next free port is retried (up to 5 rounds by default).
4. **Local tunnel**: `ssh -N -L 12"},{"id":"p25s10","text":"7.0.0.1:<local>:127.0.0.1:<remote> <alias>`; the local port is checked first (shifts automatically w"},{"id":"p25s11","text":"hen occupied, with `netstat`+`tasklist` naming the occupier). When the ssh process exits, it respawn"},{"id":"p25s12","text":"s with a backoff sequence (1s→2s→4s→8s→15s→30s cap), forever by default (`maxAttempts` configurable)"},{"id":"p25s13","text":". The tunnel deliberately does **not** pass `ClearAllForwardings` (Windows OpenSSH would clear the c"},{"id":"p25s14","text":"ommand-line `-L` along with it); exec sessions still clear config forwards.
5. **Heartbeat**: while "},{"id":"p25s15","text":"the tunnel lives, the registry's `last_heartbeat` is refreshed in-place under the lock every `heartb"},{"id":"p25s16","text":"eatSeconds` (default 120).
[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"## Security notes"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"- The tunnel and the remote dsh bind `127.0.0.1` only (dsh itself rejects `--host 0.0.0.0`)
- The pl"},{"id":"p27s2","text":"ugin never stores or transmits passwords, keys, or API keys; ssh always uses existing keys (BatchMod"},{"id":"p27s3","text":"e — no password prompts, no hangs)
- The registry records no sensitive information (see `docs/regist"},{"id":"p27s4","text":"ry-format.en.md` · 中文)
- Remote scripts only append/rewrite the registry and the systemd unit under "},{"id":"p27s5","text":"`flock`; no other writes
- The desktop/web `/remote-tunnel/*` routes go through the runtime's own ad"},{"id":"p27s6","text":"mission check (`ctx.connection.admit()` — the same Host/Origin fence plus browser-session cookie the"},{"id":"p27s7","text":" `/api` channel uses) and answer 401/403 otherwise, because they hand out a URL carrying a one-time "},{"id":"p27s8","text":"launch token. A carrier that genuinely cannot present a cookie can opt out with `auth: false` (not r"},{"id":"p27s9","text":"n. A carrier that genuinely cannot present a cookie can opt out with `auth: false` (not recommended)"}],"truncated":true}
